append.set_gripper: Timing: one native action is 10 physics steps of 4 ms (25 Hz, 40 ms per native action), so one command's 20 native actions last at most 0.8 s. Under the SDK drive limiter the jaws travel at most about 0.16 of the opening per native action: a free-air close from fully open reaches the closed floor (normalized opening about 0.185) in about 6 native actions (0.24 s), and a free-air open from closed takes about 8 (0.32 s). A command ends as soon as every named gripper is within 0.03 of its effective target, or has stopped short of it: three consecutive native actions that each moved less than 0.005 of the normalized opening. A close that stops on an object therefore ends 3 native actions (0.12 s) after the jaws stop, and reports not_reached with failure_code gripper_stalled_before_target and, for each named arm, arms.<arm>.gripper_outcome: state, commanded_opening_normalized, effective_target_opening_normalized, measured_opening_normalized, sdk_limited_drive_target_normalized (0.2 below the encoder while the jaws are held apart), ticks_used, ticks_budget and seconds_used. That is the expected result of closing on an object, not a controller fault. gripper_not_reached with state moving_at_budget means a jaw was still moving when the 20 native actions ran out. A stalled close is consistent with a grasp but does not prove one, and the normalized opening is not a calibrated jaw width: lift and observe to check retention.
append.grasp_execute: Its close stage uses the same jaw rule as set_gripper: a close that stops on the object ends 3 native actions after the jaws stop, the close stage reports status executed with reason gripper_stalled_before_target and a gripper_outcome measurement per closing arm, and the committed sequence continues to lift and verification; a stall is not a verified grasp.
